answer: Anyone can insure an identity against clonehood at a market rate, and when the identity is proved to be a clone the insurer pays out of its own reserve, which turns detection into a revenue stream for whoever performs it. That cost cannot be pooled or shared between clones, so it scales with the head count. The summit is the premium, the quartz the underwriting pool that pays on a clone proof, and the orchard the correlated funding that sets the price; the summit scales with the orchard, and the quartz only pays when the clone is actually proved.
